chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prayer behind the Imam: Do I recite behind him? He said: As for the prayer in which the recitation is not pronounced aloud, then that has been made for him, so do not recite behind him; and as for the prayer in which the recitation is pronounced aloud, then the command to pronounce it aloud is for those behind him to listen attentively. So if you hear, then listen attentively, and if you do not hear, then recite.
ai.seo_question: When should a follower recite Quran behind the Imam during loud prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'insha'ad' (listening attentively) during the Imam's loud recitation, a cornerstone of Shia fiqh that prioritizes following the Imam's lead over independent recitation. It clarifies that the command to listen applies specifically to prayers where the Imam recites aloud, such as Fajr and Maghrib, while in silent prayers like Dhuhr, the follower is exempt from reciting behind him, reflecting the juristic view that the Imam's recitation suffices for the congregation in those instances.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Salāt behind the Imam. Should I recite behind him?’ So heasws said: ‘As for the Salāt in which there is no loud recitation, so that (the recitation) is Made to be for him, therefore do not recite behind him; and as for the Salāt in which there is loud recitation, so rather it has been Commanded with the loudness for the ones behind him to be silent to it. So if you can hear, so be silent, but if you cannot hear, so recite’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about performing Salah (prayer) behind an Imam if I must do the recitation. He (the Imam) said, ‘Salah (prayer) in which recitation is not aloud, it is assigned to him. So you do not recite behind him, and for Salah (prayer) in which recitation is done aloud, he is commanded to recite aloud so people behind him remain silent; thus, if you hear him, remain silent, and if you do not hear him, then you are to recite.”’
